component: HAProxy HTTP/1 header parser, HPACK and QPACK decoders
root_cause: HAProxy's internal header lists are terminated by an entry with an empty header name, but h1_headers_to_hdr_list(), hpack_decode_frame() and qpack_decode_fs() accepted empty header field names from the peer, so a peer-sent empty name ended the list early and later headers (including Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding already seen by the parser) were dropped before forwarding.
notes: The fix commit is on the development branch; backports shipped in 2.7.3, 2.6.9, 2.5.12, 2.4.22, 2.2.29 and 2.0.31. The commit message says header lists are designed to end with an empty header field name. audit_scope covers the HTTP/1 path, which also writes the empty-name terminator; src/hpack-dec.c and src/qpack-dec.c had the same missing check for HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

component: Apache Airflow permission resource naming (FAB auth manager and airflow-core)
root_cause: resource_name() returned a dag_id unchanged when it equalled a key of RESOURCE_DETAILS_MAP (the reserved global resource names) instead of adding the 'DAG:' prefix, so a DAG named 'DAGs' mapped to the global all-DAGs permission resource and per-DAG access to it became read and edit access to every DAG.
notes: Fixed in apache-airflow-providers-fab 3.7.2; the GHSA does not state the affected range. The same commit removed the same short-circuit from airflow-core. The permission lookup that uses the resource name lives in the FAB auth manager (providers/fab/src/airflow/providers/fab/auth_manager); add it to the audit scope if needed. The Apache mailing-list thread was not read.

component: eth-infinitism account-abstraction: UserOperationLib, EntryPoint and sample VerifyingPaymaster (Solidity)
classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: UserOperationLib.pack() and VerifyingPaymaster.pack() built the hashed bytes by copying one contiguous calldata range found through the ABI .offset of the struct and of its signature field, assuming the standard ABI layout instead of encoding each field, so, because ABI decoding accepts dynamic fields in any order and at any offset, one UserOperation could produce several userOpHash values and different operations (different initCode or callData) could produce the same paymaster-signed hash.
notes: No CVE or GHSA. Disclosed on 2023-03-07 by NioLabs and others; the Alchemy post is the write-up. The fix commit ('Inconsistent userOpHash') replaced the assembly calldata copy with per-field encoding that hashes initCode, callData and paymasterAndData, and also changed contracts/core/Helpers.sol. The Alchemy post says the sample VerifyingPaymaster was not patched upstream at the time; its path in the repository was not confirmed. This is pre-release library code, so onchain is null.

root_cause: After xml-crypto verified the signature, libsaml verifySignature() selected the Assertion again by its place in the document (XPath ./*[local-name()='Assertion'] under the root) and returned that node, not the node the verified signature reference covered, so a response with a signed assertion elsewhere in the tree and an unsigned assertion in the expected place passed verification and the unsigned one was used.
notes: The fix is a merge commit ('Merge commit from fork'); ^ is its first parent on the main line. It also moves to xml-crypto 6.1.0 and takes sig.getSignedReferences()[0] as the verified content. The first fixed release is 2.10.0. The new Binding and context question reaches this only weakly; 4.46 'SAML assertions' is the direct row.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: PacketOutputStream.writeBufferEscape() escaped Buffer parameters byte by byte and put a backslash before quote bytes without looking at the connection's multi-byte client charset, so under big5, gbk, sjis, cp932 or gb18030 an attacker-chosen lead byte absorbed the inserted 0x5C as a trail byte and the following quote closed the string literal on the server.
notes: Fixed in 3.2.4, 3.3.4, 3.4.6 and 3.5.3. The fix adds charset-aware escaping (writeBufferEscapeMb and the new lib/misc/charset-mb.js) and keeps the byte-wise fast path for single-byte and UTF-8 charsets. Only client-side escaping of Buffer parameters under the five listed charsets is affected.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: html/template's JavaScript context tracker (tJS and tJSDelimited in transition.go) did not treat the backtick as a string delimiter, so inside an ES6 template literal it escaped template actions for the wrong context and action output could end the literal and inject script.
notes: The listed commits are the release-branch backports (go1.20: 20374d1, go1.19: b1e3ecf); the master commit hash was not looked up. Also fixed in go1.19.8. The fix adds stateJSBqStr, escapes backticks in JS strings and rejects actions inside template literals (GODEBUG=jstmpllitinterp=1 restores the old behavior).

component: Moby (Docker Engine) libnetwork iptables backend under firewalld
root_cause: A firewalld reload deletes all of Docker's iptables rules, replacing the whole rule set, and libnetwork restored them only by replaying callbacks registered with iptables.OnReloaded; the bridge-network isolation rules were not among the replayed pieces and callbacks of deleted networks were never removed, so after a reload isolation between bridge networks was lost and rules of deleted networks came back.
notes: Releases before 28.0.0 are affected; 28.0.0 reworked firewalld handling. The fixed backport is 25.0.13 through PR #50445, which bundles #49728 (stop re-creating rules for deleted networks) and #50443 (restore rules for the current networks on reload). The replay code in libnetwork/iptables/firewalld.go was read at v25.0.12; the bridge-driver side (which rules register reload callbacks) was not read directly. Sibling CVE-2025-54388 (published ports reachable after reload) shares the fix and is not a separate sample. Observing it needs firewalld running.

id: fleetdm/fleet#50724 SCIM group PATCH member loss (2026)
component: Fleet SCIM server, group PATCH handler
root_cause: The SCIM group Patch handler turned add and remove operations into a full member list by reading the current members from a read replica without locking, applying the operations in memory and calling ReplaceScimGroup, which deletes every member missing from the list, so a stale read or a concurrent PATCH silently removed members nobody asked to remove and group-scoped MDM profiles and certificate templates were resent to the smaller group.
notes: No CVE or GHSA. The issue calls it security-relevant (group-scoped configuration profiles and certificate templates) and labels it P2. Fixed by PR #51961 (merged 2026-09-03; milestone 4.91.1 per the issue), which adds ApplyScimGroupPatch for deltas and keeps ReplaceScimGroup for full replacement only. The first fixed release tag was not confirmed. The data heals on the next IdP push, so the bug looks intermittent.

component: Rancher legacy PRTB reconciler (Pod Security Admission permissions)
root_cause: With the aggregated-roletemplates feature off (the default), the legacy PRTB reconciler's ensurePSAPermissions() returned early once the RoleTemplate no longer granted updatepsa, so the PSA ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding it had created before were never deleted and the user kept the PSA-update permission after it was removed from the RoleTemplate, and even after the PRTB was deleted.
notes: Also fixed in 2.13.7; 2.12 and 2.11 get no patch. The fix commit was not identified. Comparing prtb_handler.go at v2.14.2 and v2.14.3 shows the change: the early return became a call to ensurePSAPermissionsDelete, which removes the stale ClusterRoleBindings and deletes the ClusterRole when nothing else binds it.

root_cause: validate_token() ran AccountTokenValidateQuery, which matched the token value through the graph's HAS_ATTRIBUTE and HAS_VALUE relationships without requiring those relationships to be active, so the history kept by the versioned graph still matched deleted tokens, and it never compared the token's expiration attribute with the current time; the fix filters on active status and rejects expired tokens.
notes: Also fixed in 1.3.9. The fix commit was not identified. Comparing core/account.py at infrahub-v1.4.4 and infrahub-v1.4.5 shows the change; I read it through fetch summaries, so the exact pre-fix branch-filter clauses were not seen. auth.py validate_api_key() calls validate_token() and then checks that the account is active; add auth.py to the audit scope. The advisory's workaround is to disable the account that owned the deleted token.
